zh-CN.AI quality changes when prompts, models,: AI quality changes when prompts, models, documents, or tools change. Evals in CI make regressions visible before users find them.
zh-CN.The practical reason this topic is getti: The practical reason this topic is getting attention in 2026 is simple: AI applications now change through prompts, retrieval data, model versions, and code. For teams shipping AI features through normal software release pipelines, the question is no longer whether the trend is interesting. The question is where it changes daily work enough to justify new process, budget, or risk review.
zh-CN.The common failure mode is testing only: The common failure mode is testing only the happy path manually after a model or prompt update. That mistake usually happens when a trend is treated as a feature checklist instead of an operating change. The technology may be new, but the weak point is often ownership, permissions, data quality, recovery, or review.
zh-CN.Before picking a vendor or writing code,: Before picking a vendor or writing code, decide which behaviors must never regress and which tradeoffs are acceptable. A clear first decision keeps the team from mixing experiments, production systems, sensitive data, and customer promises into one blurry rollout.
zh-CN.Start small: run small deterministic eva: Start small: run small deterministic eval suites on every change and broader suites before release. Keep the first version narrow enough that success and failure are both visible. That makes it easier to compare quality, cost, latency, privacy, and support load before expanding the workflow.
zh-CN.A mature workflow produces a CI check th: A mature workflow produces a CI check that scores accuracy, refusal, citation, latency, and tool safety. It should be easy for someone outside the implementation team to inspect what happened, understand why it happened, and decide whether the result is reliable enough to act on.
zh-CN.Set a review date, a measurable success: Set a review date, a measurable success criterion, and a rollback path before launch. If the AI evaluation in CI workflow does not improve the actual decision, reduce risk, save time, or create a clearer user experience, keep it in research instead of forcing it into production.
